title: "How Does the Fed Set Rates, and Can We Predict Its Next Move?"
toc: false
---

```{r}
#| include: false
# Headline numbers come from the Prediction page, which writes them when it
# renders (_quarto.yml renders it before this page).
summary_file <- "results/rq3_summary.rds"
has_results  <- file.exists(summary_file)
if (has_results) {
  rq3 <- readRDS(summary_file)
  rk  <- rq3$ranking
  fitted  <- rk[!startsWith(rk$Model, "Baseline_"), ]
  n_clear <- sum(fitted$Gap_low > 0)
  hazard_f1 <- rk$Macro_F1[rk$Model == "Hazard_Two_Step"]
  best_ml_f1 <- rk$Macro_F1[endsWith(rk$Model, "_Tuned")][1]
}
```

Eight times a year the Fed decides to cut, hold or raise interest rates.
This project predicts that decision using only information available
before each meeting.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (!has_results) {
  cat("*Render `prediction.qmd` first to fill in the results.*\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
'## Key results

- The best models score **%.2f** (macro-F1) on %d meetings since %s,
  against **%.2f** for simply repeating the last decision. %s
- What helps most is information about the Fed itself: its last
  decision, where rates are, and what markets expect.
- A simple six-input model built for policy decisions %s
',
    rq3$best_model$Macro_F1, rq3$n_test, format(rq3$test_from, "%Y"),
    rq3$baseline_f1,
    if (n_clear == 0) "The gap is too small to be sure it is real." else "",
    if (hazard_f1 >= best_ml_f1 - 0.01) "does as well as the best machine-learning model."
    else sprintf("scores %.2f, against %.2f for the best machine-learning model.", hazard_f1, best_ml_f1)
  ))
}
```

## Chapters

| Chapter | Question | Methods |
|---|---|---|
| [The data](data.qmd) | What goes in? | FRED and FOMC calendar, cleaning, publication delays |
| [The rule](rule.qmd) | How does the target relate to inflation, unemployment and financial conditions, and has that changed? | Regression, rolling coefficients, structural breaks |
| [The regimes](regimes.qmd) | Do macro conditions fall into distinct regimes? | PCA and k-means |
| [The prediction](prediction.qmd) | Using only pre-meeting information, how do model families compare at predicting cut, hold or hike? | Multinomial logit, elastic net, random forest, XGBoost, ordered probit, hazard model; expanding-window evaluation |
| [What changed](changes.qmd) | How did this grow from the course project? | Every change and its effect |

## About this project

This began as a group project for a graduate **Statistical Computing**
course in spring 2026, built with my teammates Asal D. and Zihong X. I
later came back to it to fix the limitations we had at the time: meeting
labels that were often wrong, an evaluation that rewarded always
predicting "hold", and predictors that used data before it was
published. I then extended the prediction chapter with new features and
dynamic models. Every change and its effect is documented in
[What changed](changes.qmd), and the original submission is kept as
[`v1.0-course-submission`](https://github.com/inukbaik/fomc-policy-modeling/tree/v1.0-course-submission).

*Thanks to Asal and Zihong for the original work, including The rule and
The regimes chapters.*
